evidence.quote: where Ri is the average monthly return over the next six months.
Each month from January 1965 to December 2001, we regress monthly individual stock returns on size, book-to-market ratio (BM), price momentum (J6)
Size is market capitalization at the beginning of the month.
At the beginning of each month from January 1965 (or January 1977), we independently rank firms on Size, BM, and J6 (or REV3) into 10 portfolios.
The independent variables used in the regression are the decile ranks of Size, BM and J6 (or REV3), all scaled to have a value between zero and one.
BM is book value of equity as of the previous fiscal year divided by beginning-of-month market capitalization.
IU(H) is a dummy variable that assumes a value of one for firms belonging to the IU(H) group, and zero otherwise.
In each case, a stock must be in the highest (lowest) IU tertile by all the IU variables to be included in the high (low) IU portfolio.
high-IU firms are those in the upper third by both volume and volatility each month
high-IU firms are those in the upper third by volume and volatility, and the lower third by age.
At the beginning of each month, we also independently sort stocks into three portfolios by Firm Age, Volatility and Volume.
Firm Age is defined as the number of months between event month t and the first month that a stock appears in CRSP
Return volatility (Volatility) is defined as the standard deviation of daily returns of past 25 trading days.
Trading volume (Volume) is defined as the average daily turnover in percentage over the past six months
daily turnover is the ratio of the number of shares traded each day to the number of shares outstanding at the end of the day.
Price momentum, J6, is the average monthly returns in the six months before the beginning of the current month, computed with a 1-week lag.
The displayed formula is REV_(i,t) = sum_(j=0)^3 [rev_(i,t-j) / p_(i,t-j-1)].
Our measure of earnings momentum is the average revision in the analysts’ consensus forecast over the past three months, each scaled by end-of-month price.
Earnings momentum, REV3, is the cumulative price-deflated revisions in the past three months.
Our sample consists of all firms listed on the NYSE, the AMEX and the NASDAQ during the period January 1965 through December 2001 with at least one
firms listed on NYSE/AMEX/NASDAQ between 1965 and 2001
